citations.A1: `_cache` is a module-level memo guarded only by `is None`, so the first parse is returned forever and the file is never looked at again — fix by storing the file's `os.stat` identity
citations.A2: Won't fix: a time-to-live — still stale for up to the TTL and re-parses on a clock regardless of whether the file changed
citations.A3: Won't fix: adding `reload_config()` or a manual `_cache = None` — data stays stale until some caller remembers to invoke it
citations.A4: `path` is ignored after the first call, so `get_config('other.json')` returns the first file's contents — key the cache by absolute path
citations.A5: If called from threads, wrap the stat-check-and-reload in a lock so two threads don't race on `_cache`
citations.A6: the shared mutable dict is returned directly, so any caller that mutates it poisons every later read — return a copy or a read-only mapping
citations.A8: `None` doubles as the "not loaded" sentinel, so a file containing literal `null` re-parses every call — use a private sentinel object
